I'll structure it as a mobile frame centered on the viewport with FairPrice's primary red as the key accent color throughout.

Setting up the fonts and theme first - I'm going with Nunito as the primary typeface since it's highly legible for elderly users with its friendly, rounded letterforms. Building the React component... Finishing up the olive oil list, then moving into building the app itself. Now I'm designing each screen layout—starting with the scenario screen showing the FairPrice logo, a kitchen illustration, the shopping task details with items and goals, and a prominent start button. The splash screen will have a red background with a loading animation that auto-advances after a couple seconds, and I'm planning out the remaining screens. continuing with the product details showing country of origin and reviews, then moving through the olive oil search and product screens, the shopping cart with both items, and the checkout flow including delivery address, payment method, and order confirmation with options to view orders or keep shopping.

The My Orders screen displays tabs for active, delivered, and cancelled orders with a card showing the current order status as "Preparing Order," and the Order Tracking screen breaks down the order details with a timeline of steps and estimated delivery time.

Now I'm setting up the React component structure with proper TypeScript types, making sure all JSX is properly closed, using Tailwind for styling instead of inline styles, and ensuring touch targets and font sizes are large and accessible. I'll pull in Unsplash images for the rice, olive oil, and kitchen backgrounds. I need to handle the navigation flow carefully—after adding an item to cart, the user returns to search so they can find the next product. I'm mapping out the complete screen transitions: from the splash screen through home, then into search, product results, and product details, making sure each screen has proper back navigation and cart state tracking. Setting up the component structure with imports for icons and state management for quantities and cart items... Now I'm setting up some product data with realistic Singapore prices for brown rice options, including pricing, ratings, and review counts to populate the product list. I'm finishing up the olive oil product list, then moving into building the mobile phone frame layout with Tailwind CSS—setting up a centered viewport with a status bar, scrollable content area, and fixed navigation. Writing the mobile interface... Oil results come from the olive oil search, which happens after the user adds rice to cart and returns to search. I want to add a toast notification when items are added to cart, then I'll write out the full component structure with proper state management, accessibility features, and styling optimized for elderly users with large text and FairPrice brand colors.

Writing component code... Adding product data... Continuing with the oil products array... Setting up state management for quantities and cart tracking, plus a scroll effect that resets position when the screen changes.
